title: The Upanishads and Vedanta: Brahman, Atman, and Liberation

questions.question: The word 'Vedanta' refers to:
options: The ritual portions of the Vedas
The end — both the concluding portions and the goal — of the Vedas
questions.rationale: Vedanta means the end of the Vedas in both senses: the Upanishads that close the Vedic corpus and the goal they teach — knowledge of Brahman.

questions.question: According to the traditional Muktika list, how many Upanishads are there?
questions.rationale: The Muktika canon counts 108 Upanishads, of which about 13 are treated as philosophically principal.

questions.question: The mahavakya 'Tat tvam asi' — That thou art — comes from which Upanishad?
questions.rationale: 'Tat tvam asi' is Chandogya's great sentence; 'Aham brahmasmi' is Brihadaranyaka's, 'Prajnanam brahma' Aitareya's, and 'Ayam atma brahma' Mandukya's.

questions.question: Brahman is classically described as:
questions.rationale: The Upanishads characterise the sole ultimate reality as existence, consciousness, and bliss; the Atman, the innermost self, is identical with it.

questions.question: The Upanishadic pivot away from the ritual Vedas is the claim that liberation comes through:
options: Direct knowledge (jnana) of the identity of Atman and Brahman
questions.rationale: Knowledge replaces sacrifice: avidya and maya conceal the ever-present identity, and moksha dawns when jnana dissolves the ignorance.

questions.question: Which trio summarises Shankara's Advaita?
options: Brahma satyam, jagat mithya, jivo brahmaiva naparah
questions.rationale: Brahman alone is real, the world is appearance, and the soul is none other than Brahman — the core of Shankara's (788–820 CE) non-dualism.

questions.question: The doctrine of ajativada — that nothing ever truly originates — is associated with:
questions.rationale: Gaudapada's Mandukya Karika teaches ajativada; he stands at the head of the Advaita line, two teachers before Shankara.

questions.question: Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita holds that souls and matter are:
options: Real as the body and modes of a Brahman with attributes
Eternal and wholly independent of God
questions.rationale: For Ramanuja (1017–1137), one saguna Brahman exists, with souls and matter as its real but dependent body — hence 'qualified non-dualism'.

questions.question: Madhva's five eternal differences (pancha-bheda) include:
options: God differs from soul, God from matter, souls from one another, souls from matter, and matter from matter
questions.rationale: Dvaita's realism posits five irreducible differences across God, souls, and matter; Vishnu is supreme and liberation comes through devotion.

questions.question: Who carried Vedanta to the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893?
questions.rationale: Vivekananda's 1893 Chicago address announced the harmony of religions and launched modern Neo-Vedanta and the Ramakrishna Mission.
